item.title: CREMA: Collinear Resonance for Exotic Molecules and Atoms
item.description: arXiv:2610.30522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Collinear Resonance for Exotic Molecules and Atoms (CREMA) setup has been developed and commissioned at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Laboratory for Nuclear Science. The instrument combines the Doppler-suppressed resolution of the collinear fast-beam geometry with the selectivity of resonance ionization, for precision measurements of hyperfine structure and isotope shifts in atoms and molecules. We describe the setup, including the ion-optical simulations in which a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm provided the starting settings for the beam transport, and report commissioning measurements of the hyperfine structure of 133Cs. The extracted hyperfine constants agree with literature values within one standard deviation, demonstrating the operational readiness of the setup. CREMA mirrors the Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy Experiment at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams and serves as its offline counterpart for the development of laser ionization schemes and techniques for future studies of exotic atoms and molecules.

item.title: Lifetime of the singly charged $^{229}$Th nuclear isomer
item.description: arXiv:2610.31009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nucleus of thorium-229 ($^{229}$Th) has an exceptionally low-energy isomeric state ($^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th). Because its excitation energy is close to the energy levels of valence electrons, the lifetime of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th varies substantially depending on its electronic state. Although internal conversion and radiative decay were recently observed, the electronic bridge decay of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th, a higher-order decay process through an electronic transition, has not yet been confirmed. A promising candidate to search for this decay channel is singly charged $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th$^+$ in the electronic ground state. Here we produce $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th$^+$ by a charge exchange reaction in an ion trap and detect the isomers through measuring the electrons emitted from internal conversion processes. We determined the half-life of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th$^+$ to be 0.46(8) s. Our result differs by several orders of magnitude from the half-lives of internal conversion and radiative decay, indirectly suggesting the existence of the electronic bridge decay of $^{229\mathrm{m}}$Th. This will enable the direct observation and further investigation of the electronic bridge process, which will contribute to understanding nuclear-electron interactions and accelerating nuclear deexcitation in the operation of a thorium-based nuclear clock.

item.title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Weed

item.title: Unfolding the low-energy reactor neutrino flux from CE$\nu$NS data with a finite Dirac sum
item.description: arXiv:2608.16107v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a novel method to analyze coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) data to extract the reactor antineutrino spectrum below the inverse beta decay threshold of 1.8 MeV, where it remains unmeasured. Adapting halo-independent analysis techniques developed for direct dark matter detection, we show how to obtain a best-fit and a pointwise confidence band for the integrated neutrino flux, without assuming a parametric form or smoothness prior for the spectrum. In our approach, which follows from convex geometry arguments, the differential neutrino rate is written as a linear combination of Dirac delta functions -- a finite Dirac sum (FDS) -- with a maximum number of terms determined by the number of data points. We apply our "FDS method" to mock CE$\nu$NS data for a low-threshold Ge detector and compare it with Tikhonov-regularized unfolding.
item.dc:creator: Muping Chen, Graciela Gelmini, Danny Marfatia, Koichiro Yasuda

item.title: Probing imperfect axions with nuclear clocks
item.description: arXiv:2610.30238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks can probe departures from the Peccei-Quinn (PQ) solution to the strong CP problem. Explicit PQ breaking or additional CP-violating interactions can shift the minimum of the axion potential and generate CP-violating couplings to matter, inducing a clock response linear in the axion field. We investigate explicit PQ breaking and quark chromo-electric dipole operators as representative realizations of these \textit{imperfect axion} scenarios, consistent with electric dipole moment constraints. For axion dark matter, the linear signal oscillates at the Compton frequency and can dominate the quadratic response. Even without axion dark matter, the Earth can source a static axion field, enabling fifth-force searches with nuclear clocks.
item.dc:creator: Salvatore Bottaro, Andrea Caputo, Gilad Perez, Yotam Soreq, Alfredo Stanzione

item.title: Track finding and particle identification performance with particle physics foundation models
item.description: arXiv:2610.31180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern high energy nuclear and particle physics experiments produce large amounts of sparse data that must be reduced significantly in size before performing physics analysis. Recently, there has been an effort to evaluate Foundation Models as a potential tool for performing data analysis. These models have been shown to learn features in high dimensional datasets based on the multi-modal data they are trained on. To show their effectiveness at performing complex pattern recognition tasks, such as reconstructing charged particles in a magnetic field, we evaluated the performance of a Foundation Model based reconstruction on several downstream tasks with a dataset composed of spacepoints in a Time Projection Chamber. We show that the performance of the Foundation Model based data analysis significantly improves upon that of traditional methods, and furthermore can be adapted to learn additional tasks that are not necessarily related to the initial training objective.

item.title: Remarks on MAMI's recent determination of $B_{\Lambda}({_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H})$
item.description: arXiv:2604.18259v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A recent report on ${^7{\rm Li}}(e,e'K^+)$ electroproduction runs by the A1 collaboration at the Mainz Microtron (MAMI) assigns a sharp pion-momentum line at $p_{\pi^-}\approx 113.8\pm 0.1$ MeV/c to ${_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H}\to\pi^-+{^3{\rm He}}$ weak decay, resulting in exceptionally large ${_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H}$ binding-energy $B_{\Lambda}({_{\Lambda}^3}{\rm H})=0.523\pm 0.013\pm 0.075$ MeV. Here I discuss an alternative interpretation of the observed sharp line in terms of ${_{\Lambda}^7}{\rm He}_{\rm g.s.}\to\pi^-+{^7{\rm Li}}(E_{\rm x}=478$ keV) weak decay and its implications for $B_{\Lambda}({_{\Lambda}^7}{\rm He})$.
item.dc:creator: Avraham Gal

item.title: \textit{Ab initio} no-core shell model calculations of the electric dipole polarizabilities and photoabsorption cross sections of the $A=3$ mirror nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.29711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present \textit{ab initio} no-core shell-model calculations of the electric dipole ($E1$) polarizabilities and photoabsorption cross sections of the $A=3$ mirror nuclei $^3$H and $^3$He using the Daejeon16 nucleon-nucleon interaction. The polarizabilities are obtained by direct summation over discretized continuum states in the harmonic-oscillator basis, while the same spectral information is used to reconstruct the cross sections. This work provides the first extension of the approach from the spin-zero $^4$He to nonzero-spin nuclei by calculating the $1/2^-$ and $3/2^-$ final-state contributions separately and demonstrating their model-space convergence. In both nuclei, the $3/2^-$ contribution is approximately twice the $1/2^-$ contribution. After quantifying finite-basis and excitation-energy-truncation uncertainties, we identify a clear difference between the mirror polarizabilities, induced entirely by the Coulomb interaction because the Daejeon16 interaction is isospin symmetric. The reconstructed cross sections remain stable under variations of the inversion parameters of the Lorentz integral transform and exhibit the same angular-momentum hierarchy. These results extend the discretized-continuum approach to integrated and energy-resolved $E1$ observables in nonzero-spin nuclei with multiple final-state angular momenta.
